instructions: Slice the 3 zucchini into rounds about 1/4 inch thick. Chop 1/4 cup of the parsley. Grate the halloumi.
Crack the 6 eggs into a bowl, add 1/4 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper and beat until no streaks of white are left.
Melt the butter in a large, deep skillet with a lid over medium heat. Add the zucchini, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the remaining 1/4 tsp pepper.
Cook for 10 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes, until the zucchini is soft and golden at the edges.
Stir in the parsley. Turn the heat to medium-low, pour the eggs evenly over the zucchini, and sprinkle the halloumi over the top.
Cover and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the eggs are set and there is no wet egg left on top.
Serve in wedges straight from the skillet.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Greek Boston's Avga Kolokithia (no rating shown) is the lead: zucchini cooked in butter with parsley, then beaten eggs and a grated cheese on top, covered until set. The Cyprus Food Museum version fries the zucchini in olive oil and finishes with grated halloumi. To fit about 30 minutes the zucchini is cut into thin rounds and cooked uncovered for 10 minutes (the lead cooks thick slices covered for 30), the butter is cut from 1/2 cup to 4 tbsp, and halloumi from the Cyprus version is the cheese so it stays vegetarian. The lead's optional diced tomatoes were left out.
